hints.title: Bottom-Up Ordering Obstacle
hints.text: Bottom-up level ordering requires returning leaf levels first and the root level last. Can you perform a top-down level-by-level traversal and invert the resulting tier list at the end?

hints.title: Reversed Tier Invariant
hints.text: A bottom-up level traversal produces the exact reverse sequence of the top-down level-by-level traversal.

hints.title: Top-Down BFS with Post-Reversal
hints.text: Traverse each level using a queue from top to bottom, recording each level's node values into a list. Append each level list to the master list. Reverse the master list before returning.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: number of nodes in tree (0 <= N <= 2000)
W: maximum level width of tree
complexity.notes: Standard level order queue traversal followed by inverting the outer list in O(N) total time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Depth-first collection requires manual tracking and re-indexing of tiers.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Auxiliary queue memory proportional to maximum tree width.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Using standard BFS and inverting the outer array in O(height) time.
